title: Law is the floor, ethics is the ceiling
sources: UPSC CSE syllabus, GS Paper IV
Lexicon / standard GS4 texts on ethics and human interface

quiz.q: Which statement best describes the link between law and ethics?
quiz.why: Right. Law is often called the minimum of ethics.

lines.say: Is something right just because it's legal?
Ethics asks a bigger question than the law does.

beats.say: Is something right just because it's legal? Ethics asks a bigger question than the law does.

lines.say: Law tells you the minimum you must do.
Ethics asks what is right, even where the law is silent.

data.text: Law sets the minimum. Ethics asks what is right beyond it.

beats.say: Law tells you the minimum you must do. Ethics asks what is right, even where the law is silent.

lines.say: Look at the intention behind an act, and the means used.
And at its consequences, for everyone affected.

beats.say: Look at the intention behind an act, and the means used. And at its consequences, for everyone affected.

lines.say: Gandhi held that good ends never justify bad means.
He said the means are like a seed, and the end, the tree.

data.text: "The means may be likened to a seed, the end to a tree."
